statement_summary: One CSF-aligned program meeting each division's primary regulation
Group CISO accountable; Qualified Individual, COPPA coordinator, and HIPAA officials designated in writing
Annual SP 800-30 risk analysis per division and after material changes; roll-up to group
Risk acceptance authority by level; High risks of harm to children or education access must be treated
Division supplements may not weaken group policy; re-align within 90 days; annual attestation
Common control inheritance documented per division system and confirmed each year
Sanctions proportionate to intent and harm, documented by HR
Written agreements with safeguards, notice times, and right to assess for every service provider, including sister divisions; annual assessment
Annual assessment of common controls and division samples; annual penetration tests and six-monthly vulnerability assessments
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Security documentation retained 6 years
AI systems registered and approved under the Group AI Standard before deployment or material change
Qualified Individual reports in writing at least annually to the college board of trustees; quarterly report to the board risk committee
Unique identity in SYS-G1 for every workforce user; legacy domains migrated by 2027-03-31
Role-based least privilege; education records limited to legitimate educational interest
MFA for all workforce and students; phishing-resistant for administrators
Service accounts owned, governed, rotated every 90 days, certified
Access disabled within 4 hours of termination
Quarterly access certification including privileged and service accounts
Just-in-time privileged access through PAM with recording
Lockout, workstation lock, and session timeouts
Sealed, tested break-glass accounts
Customer tenant access only per ticket, customer-approved, time-limited, through PAM; no standing cross-tenant access
Vendor remote maintenance through PAM; no persistent tunnels
Student MFA; bank detail changes with fresh MFA and out-of-band confirmation; MFA offered to families and patients
Unique, rotated local administrator passwords
Report suspected incidents to the SOC within 1 hour
One group severity scale
Incident log with legally relevant dates
Designated officials make and document regulatory determinations with counsel
Notification matrix maintained and updated within 30 days of changes
Intercompany notice within 24 hours; plan deadlines from the earliest group knowledge
Disclosure committee convened within 24 hours of Severity 1
Ransom decisions by the board risk committee with counsel, insurer, and OFAC check
Out-of-band communications and printed binders
Lessons learned within 14 days; weaknesses to the POA&M
Quarterly playbook tests; annual cross-division tabletop with notifications
Plan covers the seven elements of 314.4(h)
Every shared data set has an owner, class, governing law, and purpose in the catalog
Encryption in transit and at rest; Qualified Individual approves compensating controls
Data flows between divisions need written approval by both data owners with legal basis and minimum fields
Treatment records stay within Student Health except for treatment, consent, or the owning institution's direction
FAFSA and FTI-derived data used only for aid administration; never as model inputs
Children's information only under district authorization or parental consent; deleted within 90 days after contract end
Customer information disposed of within 2 years after last use unless needed; SP 800-88 sanitization
Clinic records flagged PHI or FERPA record, with owning institution
Restricted data only in approved AI tools with no-training terms
Look up records only when the job requires it
Never share credentials; report unexpected MFA prompts and verification lures
Approved generative AI tools only; no Restricted data in unapproved tools
AI outputs about people are prompts for human review, never decisions
Record clinic visits only after all-party consent captured in the EHR
